commit.message:
Pull Fundraiser 'raised' total from the campaign's on-chain address

The progress bar was hardcoded to 0% with a comment promising a future
enhancement. Matched Agora's approach: read funded_txo_sum directly
from the campaign's `w` address via Esplora, no kind 8333 verification
needed. Donations count whether or not the donor published a Nostr
receipt, and the number doesn't regress when the beneficiary spends.

New useCampaignDonations hook wraps the Esplora address lookup + BTC
price, returning {totalSats, btcPrice}. CampaignContent uses it for a
new CampaignProgress block that renders 'raised $X of $Y goal' when a
goal is set, or just 'raised $X' when there's no goal but there are
on-chain donations.

Silent-payment-only campaigns continue to show the 'totals are not
public' notice (the address has no public aggregate by design).

NIP.md updated to drop the stale 'empty progress bar' caveat.

Reorders the Donate dialog so the QR + copyable URI sit immediately

Scanning from another device is the most visual affordance and reads
first; the in-app/native-wallet actions act as alternatives beneath it.

commit.message:
Zap Fundraisers from Ditto's built-in wallet

The action-bar zap button on a kind 33863 campaign post used to derive
the Taproot address from the campaign author's pubkey and send to that.
That's wrong: the spec says donations go to the address declared in the
campaign's `w` tag, which may be a separate cold wallet, a multisig,
or a silent-payment code \u2014 not the author's identity-derived P2TR.

This change wires campaigns through their declared endpoint:

- New useCampaignZap hook. Mirrors useOnchainZap but sends to the
  campaign's `w` value, drops the self-zap guard (donating to your
  own campaign is legitimate), and publishes a kind 8333 receipt in
  the campaign-wallet form per NIP.md: `i`, `amount`, `a`, `K`,
  `alt`. No `p` tags \u2014 campaigns aren't Nostr-identity recipients.
  When the campaign declares both rails it prefers on-chain (the
  spec's default and the only one that contributes to public totals).
  Silent-payment donations broadcast via buildUnsignedSilentPaymentPsbt
  and intentionally publish no Nostr event, preserving SP unlinkability.

- OnchainZapContent takes an optional `campaign` prop that routes the
  send through useCampaignZap instead of useOnchainZap. Both hooks are
  always instantiated (rules of hooks); useCampaignZap accepts `null`
  and short-circuits when the caller isn't in campaign mode.

- ZapDialog detects target.kind === 33863, parses the campaign, hides
  the Lightning tab (kind 33863 has no LNURL endpoint), retitles the
  dialog to 'Donate to {title}', bypasses the self-zap check for
  campaign creators, and forwards the parsed campaign down.

- ZapSuccessScreen accepts an optional recipientLabel so campaign
  donations read 'Donation sent \u2192 {campaign title}' instead of
  'Bitcoin sent \u2192 @author'.

- The Donate dialog on the campaign detail page gains a primary 'Zap'
  button that opens ZapDialog (hidden when the user lacks a PSBT-
  capable signer). 'Open in Wallet' is renamed to 'Open native wallet'
  for clarity now that an in-app Zap option exists alongside it.

commit.message:
Fix Donate dialog overflow when bip21 URI is wide

DialogContent uses CSS grid for its children. Grid auto-track sizing
respects the min-content of descendants — so the long bip21 URI inside
the copyable input pushed the column wider than the dialog, dragging
the QR, input, and 'Open in Wallet' button past the right edge.

Adding min-w-0 to the flex containers (both the copyable button and
the truncating span inside it) lets the grid track actually honor the
dialog's max-width, and the URI ellipsis-truncates as intended.

commit.message:
Move Fundraiser donate UI into a Donate-button dialog

The inline donate panel was overstepping — too much surface area on the
detail page before the donor even decided to give, and the split
on-chain / silent-payment rows showed strings that disagreed with the
QR contents byte-for-byte.

Replace it with a single 'Donate' button that opens a dialog containing:

- the BIP-21 QR,
- exactly one copyable input whose value is the same URI encoded in the
  QR (so the copy affordance and the scan affordance can never drift),
- the 'Open in Wallet' action,
- and the silent-payment privacy note when an sp1 endpoint is present.

The wallet-mode label on the input is gone — donors don't need to know
whether a campaign is on-chain, silent-payment, or both. The combined
BIP-21 URI handles all three cases transparently (legacy wallets read
the on-chain address; BIP-352-aware wallets pick up the ?sp= extension).

commit.message:
Add donate QR + 'Open in Wallet' to Fundraiser detail page

The wallet-mode pill on the campaign card was visual noise — donors don't
need to know whether a campaign is on-chain, silent-payment, or both
before they engage with it. The combined BIP-21 QR transparently handles
all three modes (legacy wallets read the on-chain address; BIP-352-aware
wallets pick up the `?sp=` extension), so the pill carried no useful
information and is removed.

In its place, the expanded detail page now renders a donate panel with:

- A BIP-21 QR code built from the campaign's `w` endpoint(s), per the
  spec's combined-URI rules (`bitcoin:bc1…?sp=sp1…` when both are
  declared, single-rail otherwise).
- An 'Open in Wallet' button that hands the URI to `openUrl()` — on
  native it presents the OS share sheet, on the web it navigates to the
  `bitcoin:` URI so a registered desktop wallet can pick it up.
- Copyable rows for the raw on-chain address and/or silent-payment code
  so donors who prefer one rail can grab it without scanning.
- A short privacy note when an SP endpoint is present, mirroring the
  spec's guidance that SP donations are unlinkable by design and
  intentionally absent from any public total.

The feed card stays minimal — just banner, Fundraiser pill, title,
summary, goal, and meta. Donors land on the panel by tapping through
to the campaign's naddr page.

commit.message:
Support Agora Fundraisers (kind 33863)

Render Agora's self-authored Bitcoin fundraising campaigns wherever Ditto
shows Nostr content: home and profile feeds, the campaign's naddr detail
page, quote embeds, and NIP-22 comment context.

- lib/campaign.ts parses kind 33863 into a typed ParsedCampaign, validating
  the bech32(m) checksum of every on-chain w endpoint and accepting at most
  one endpoint per mode (on-chain / silent payment), per the spec.
- CampaignContent renders the feed card (banner, title, summary, wallet
  pill, country + deadline meta) and an expanded variant for the detail
  page that pipes the markdown story through ArticleContent's renderer.
- EmbeddedNaddr dispatches kind 33863 to a compact card with banner +
  Fundraiser pill so quote embeds read at a glance.
- NoteCard, PostDetailPage, kindLabels, CommentContext, feedUtils,
  extraKinds, AppContext, schemas, App.tsx, and TestApp all gain the
  matching 33863 entry. feedIncludeCampaigns defaults on so campaigns
  appear in home and profile feeds out of the box.
- Comment threads anchored to a campaign coordinate read 'Commenting on
  @author's fundraiser', mirroring the highlight pattern.
- NIP.md documents the kind alongside Ditto's other supported community
  kinds, copying the protocol spec from Agora's NIP.md and noting that
  Ditto intentionally omits donation flows, on-chain verification, and
  agora.moderation labels — those belong to Agora itself.

commit.message:
Honor BIP-21 sp= silent-payment parameter in Send QR scanner

The Send dialog's QR handler stripped the BIP-21 query string entirely,
so scanning a 'bitcoin:bc1q…?sp=sp1q…' URI silently dropped the silent
payment recipient and used only the on-chain fallback.

Parse the query with URLSearchParams and, when an 'sp=' parameter
decodes as a valid BIP-352 address, prefer it over the on-chain
fallback. URIs with no 'sp=' (or an invalid one) keep the previous
fallback behavior.
